draft.title: Evidence of climate change
card: Climate is the pattern of weather in a place over many years. Scientists look for long-term trends in measurements, not one hot day or one cold year.
Air and ocean temperatures have risen over the past century. Warmer water also expands, and melting land ice adds water to the sea, so sea levels are rising.
Sea ice and glaciers are shrinking. Satellite images and measurements taken over many years show the loss.
Many species are moving to cooler places, such as higher up mountains or further from the equator. Together, these different kinds of evidence show the climate is changing.
draft.remember: Many long-term measurements point the same way: the climate is changing.

a.q: Which observation is the best evidence that the climate is changing?
opts: Average ocean temperatures have risen over many decades
Sydney had one very hot week last summer
A cold winter hit Hobart this year
A storm flooded a town in Queensland last month
a.why: Climate is a long-term pattern, so a trend over many decades is strong evidence. One hot week, one cold winter or one storm is weather, and a single event cannot show a long-term change.
a.clue: Climate is about patterns over many years.

b.q: Alpine plants on a mountain in Tasmania are now found 100 metres higher than they were 50 years ago. What does this most likely show?
opts: Species are moving to cooler places as temperatures rise
Sea levels around Tasmania have fallen
Glaciers on the mountain have grown larger
The mountain has become cooler over 50 years
b.why: Plants growing higher up are moving to cooler ground, which fits a warming climate. A cooler mountain would not push plants uphill, so that option reverses the cause.
b.clue: Higher up a mountain, the air is cooler.

a.best: Average ocean temperatures have risen over many decades

b.best: Species are moving to cooler places as temperatures rise

proposal.title: Evidence of climate change
card: Climate is the pattern of weather in a place over many years. Scientists look for long-term trends in measurements, not one hot day or one cold year.
Air and ocean temperatures have risen over the past century. Warmer water also expands, and melting land ice adds water to the sea, so sea levels are rising.
Sea ice and glaciers are shrinking. Satellite images and measurements taken over many years show the loss.
Many species are moving to cooler places as their old homes warm. Some move higher up mountains, where the air is cooler, and some move further from the equator.
proposal.remember: Many long-term measurements point the same way: the climate is changing.

a.q: Which observation is the best evidence that the climate is changing?
opts: Average ocean temperatures have risen over many decades
Sydney had one very hot week last summer
A cold winter hit Hobart this year
A storm flooded a town in Queensland last month
a.why: Climate is a long-term pattern, so a trend over many decades is strong evidence. One hot week, one cold winter or one storm is weather, and a single event cannot show a long-term change.
a.clue: Climate is about patterns over many years.

b.q: Alpine plants on a mountain in Tasmania now grow 100 metres higher than they did 50 years ago. What is the most likely reason?
opts: Their lower slopes have become too warm for them
Their lower slopes have become too cold for them
Growing glaciers have covered their lower slopes
Cooler summers now let them grow further uphill
b.why: Air higher up a mountain is cooler, so plants that need cold conditions shift uphill as the lower slopes warm. Saying the lower slopes became too cold reverses the cause: cooling would let the plants spread downhill, not push them up. Glaciers are shrinking and temperatures are rising, so the other two options do not fit the evidence.
b.clue: Think about which way temperatures have moved and where cooler air is found.
